messages:
Olivia Chan: Heads up — Finance flagged a 12% delta between ACME's marketplace consumption report and our internal ledger for billing window 2026-03-18 00:00-23:59. Compare is on raw units, not dollars. Can partnerships + eng quickly eyeball?
Samir Patel: On it. Which file/time range?
Olivia Chan: The marketplace webhook batch for 2026-03-18 23:45 UTC (batch_id: batch-20260318-2345). ACME sent ~1.12M units, our aggregator shows ~990k.
Maria Gomez: Pulling the raw webhook archive now. I see their payloads in s3://partners/acme/inbound/2026-03-18/*.gz — starting to decompress.
usage-ingest-bot: ingest-processor v2.4 deployed 2026-03-18T22:50Z — processed 1,234 files from partners queue.
Samir Patel: Quick sanity checks: 1) seqno continuity 2) duplicate suppression 3) timezone conversion (ACME reports local TZ). Maria, can you grep for out-of-order seq?
Maria Gomez: Found a cluster of late-arriving events with seq_no gaps around seq 987650-987665. A few arrive with timestamp 2026-03-18T23:59:59-08:00 (PST). Looks like our ingestion normalized to UTC but the batch assignment used UTC midnight rounding which may have moved some events to next day.
Ryan Billing: If events drifted into next day we could undercount the 03-18 window. Finance wants a reconciliation plan before EoD.
Samir Patel: Shared a quick query to check how many events were assigned to 03-19 due to TZ rounding:
```
SELECT count(*) FROM partner_events
WHERE partner='acme' AND event_time >= '2026-03-18' AND event_time < '2026-03-19'
AND ingestion_time_partition = '2026-03-19';
```
Samir Patel: Running that now.
Maria Gomez: Also seeing a small set of duplicate event_ids where acme retried with new payloads. Our dedupe key is (partner, event_id). Some retries had different event_id because their client reissued.
Olivia Chan: Do we have a canonical fallback? If partner changed event_id on retry we might count both.
Samir Patel: We agreed to prefer partner_provided_id; if missing, use hash(payload). I'll check if the changed id bypassed dedupe.
usage-ingest-bot: query result: 14,350 events assigned to 2026-03-19 partition that have event_time within 2026-03-18 UTC window.
Maria Gomez: That explains ~1.15% of delta. Still leaves ~10.85% unexplained.
Samir Patel: Next suspect: ACME changed unit granularity for one SKU (switched from seconds -> minutes) on 2026-03-18 20:00 local. If we didn't apply their new multiplier, counts diverge. Maria, can you check SKU "acme.compute.small" unit metadata?
Maria Gomez: Found commit in partner-metadata: acme: {'compute.small': {'unit': 'seconds', 'multiplier': 1}} then at 2026-03-18T20:02:12-07:00 changed to {'unit':'minutes','multiplier':60}. Our metadata sync job runs hourly — there's a chance it missed the 20:02 change until 21:00.
Olivia Chan: If ACME sent data measured after 20:02 but we applied old multiplier, we'd undercount by ~60x for that SKU — but that would be a huge delta for the subset of traffic. Does that align with which SKUs changed?
Maria Gomez: Only ~0.4% of total units are compute.small; even a multiplier mismatch wouldn't produce 10% across all SKUs. So it's part of the answer but not all.
Samir Patel: Another angle: did any ingestion workers return 5xx and event move to DLQ and get reprocessed with altered timestamps? Check DLQ replay logs between 22:40-23:59Z.
Maria Gomez: DLQ replay shows 72k events replayed; 60% replayed with original event_time preserved, 40% had ingestion_time updated but event_time preserved. Not seeing mass timestamp rewrites.
Ryan Billing: Finance also called out a set of credits we issued yesterday to a subset of ACME customers — could those be double-applied in our ledger?
Olivia Chan: Good point. Did the credits pipeline affect reporting? The crediting flow writes a compensating negative usage row that should be excluded from partner comparators. If filters missed it, numbers diverge.
Samir Patel: I'll run a diff that excludes any rows with adjustment_type IS NOT NULL.
Samir Patel: Running diff now — excluding adjustments reduces the gap by ~3.9%.
Maria Gomez: So far: TZ rounding 1.15% + credits filter 3.9% + metadata multiplier 0.4% = ~5.45%. Still ~6.5% left.
Olivia Chan: Could there be marketplace-side throttling or sampling? ACME's marketplace contract has a sampling clause for high throughput hours — if they sample then extrapolate, their reported numbers could differ from raw events. Partners-team, can you ask ACME what their marketplace aggregation logic was on 03-18 evening?
partners-team: Reaching out. Sending a quick message: "Can you confirm if marketplace reports were sampled/extrapolated or if any SKU multipliers changed during 03-18 PST evening? Also please share the raw webhook id range for 2345 batch."
partners-team: ACME response (1m): "We performed a late resample for high-ingress window starting 03-18T20:00 PST due to spikes; reported values are extrapolated. Full raw ingestion logs available at https://acme.logs/2026-03-18. Also we rotated event_id generator between 23:50-23:56 which may have produced non-dedupable ids."
Samir Patel: That explains sampling/extrapolation. We need to reconcile using raw logs, not their reported aggregated values. Two action tracks: 1) short-term: compute corrected usage by replaying raw webhooks and applying latest multipliers and dedupe rules (owner: Maria + Samir) 2) medium-term: add a contract clause to marketplace connector to submit raw event counts alongside extrapolated totals and include a sampling flag in the feed (owner: partnerships/legal).
Maria Gomez: For the short-term replay I'll: a) copy raw files to staging b) apply current metadata multipliers c) run dedupe using (client_id, original_event_id OR payload_hash) d) re-emit partition assignments into reconciliation job. ETA 3h.
Olivia Chan: Please also tag finance and send a provisional corrected number as soon as available. Finance needs a revised invoice draft.
Ryan Billing: I'll hold the invoice finalization until we have the corrected figure. If replay takes longer than 3h, send an interim note to finance.
Samir Patel: I pushed a quick query to surface top 10 SKUs by unit delta so we can prioritize:
```
SELECT sku, sum(partner_units) as partner_units, sum(our_units) as our_units, (sum(partner_units)-sum(our_units))/sum(partner_units) as pct_diff
FROM reconciliation_view
WHERE partner='acme' AND invoice_day='2026-03-18'
GROUP BY sku
ORDER BY pct_diff DESC
LIMIT 10;
```
Samir Patel: Sharing results: top SKU diffs are: acme.storage.large (6.2% of gap), acme.analytics.pro (2.5%), acme.network.bandwidth (1.1%), others spread small.
Maria Gomez: Starting the replay now. I'll post progress and any blockers.
Olivia Chan: Thanks. Once Maria posts corrected counts, we'll prepare a short customer-facing note explaining "extrapolation vs raw counts" and propose the metadata contract. Keep me looped. :thumbsup:
partners-team: ACME acknowledged and agreed to provide raw event_id mapping file and sampling flag for future exports.
usage-ingest-bot: staging-replay job started: job_id replay-486000-1. Logs stream at https://ci.redwood/replays/replay-486000-1
Maria Gomez: update +1h: replay completed on staging, preliminary corrected delta down to 0.8%. Sending sanitized reconcile CSV to finance and acme.
Olivia Chan: Huge — excellent work. Next steps: 1) partners to negotiate feed contract changes (sampling flag + raw counts) 2) eng to add hourly metadata sync alert 3) billing to hold final invoice until sign-off. Owners: partnerships, eng, finance.
Samir Patel: I'll open an eng ticket for metadata sync alert (ENG-5698) and a dedupe robustness follow-up (ENG-5699).
Ryan Billing: Finance will wait for final confirm. Thanks team.
Olivia Chan: Closing the loop here — will follow up with customer comms draft shortly. :heart:
